chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
"There is no harm in hastening the last (Isha) prayer during travel before the twilight (shafaq) disappears."

key_terms.اَلشَّفَقُ: Twilight (the red glow in the sky after sunset)

ai.seo_question: When can a traveler perform the Isha prayer early according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Shaykh al-Tusi records this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishing the permissibility of offering the late Isha prayer early during travel, specifically before the fading of the red twilight (*shafaq*). This ruling highlights the practical flexibility (*rukhsah*) granted to travelers in Shia jurisprudence to ease religious obligations amidst the fatigue of journeying, distinguishing it from the standard time for Isha in settled residence.
